AssetsTenant.description: The caller's tenant as this service knows it.

created_at.description: When this service learned of the tenant, by the database clock.

tenant_id.description: The tenant to bind the gateway to.

BucketInterval.description:
A bucket length of the semantic API: whole local minutes, hours, days, Monday weeks and
months of the requested time zone, or the whole range.

CodeSent.description: The answer to `send_code`, the same whether or not a user has the address.

expires_in_secs.description: How long the code is valid, in seconds.

resend_after_secs.description: How long to wait before asking for another code, in seconds.

CreateDevice.description: The body of `POST /api/assets/v1/devices`. Unknown fields are refused.

hardware_id.description: The gateway that polls it: one currently bound to the caller's tenant.

model_id.description: One of the caller's tenant's device models.

name.description: The new device's name, unique in the tenant (see [`Device::name`]).

transport.description: `modbus_tcp`: Modbus TCP to the device. `rtu_over_tcp`: RTU frames over TCP to an RS485 converter; the devices behind one converter (the same host and port on one gateway) share its connection, so they all use this transport and each has its own unit ID.

CreateDeviceModel.description: The body of `POST /api/assets/v1/device-models`. Unknown fields are refused.

name.description: The new model's name, unique in the tenant (see [`DeviceModel::name`]).

points.description: The data points, at most 1000, in order; may be empty.

CreateTenant.description: The body of `POST /api/identity/v1/tenants`. Unknown fields are ignored.

name.description:
What people call the tenant: 1 to 100 characters after trimming, without control or
format characters or line and paragraph separators.

CumulativeCheck.description: The cumulative check over the window read around the range.

drops.description: How often the value fell, rose, and was compared with the one before.

oneOf.description:
The tenant the session acts in, with the user's role there; `null` when it acts in none:
none was picked yet, or the user is no longer a member of it.

email.description: The address the user logs in with; `null` for a user who cannot log in by email.

platform_admin.description: Whether the user is a platform administrator (A2), independent of any tenant.

tenants.description:
Every tenant the user belongs to, by name; switch with
`PUT /api/identity/v1/sessions/current/tenant`.

DataStatus.description: Whether a series had readings in the range.

Device.description: A device: a Modbus endpoint one of the tenant's gateways polls with one of its models.

created_at.description: When the device was created, by the database clock.

device_id.description: The device's ID; telemetry names the device by it.

hardware_id.description:
The hardware ID of the gateway that polls the device, bound to the tenant; never
changed after creation.

host.description:
The IP address or DNS name of the device, or of the converter it is behind; never the
gateway itself (a loopback address or `localhost`).

model_id.description: The device model the gateway reads the device with; never changed after creation.

name.description:
The name, unique in the tenant, never changed after creation: 1-40 lowercase letters or
digits in groups joined by single hyphens, starting with a letter (the naming rule of
models).

poll_interval_ms.description:
How often the gateway polls the device, in milliseconds: 1000 (1 s) to 86400000
(1 day); 60000 (1 minute) when a request leaves it out. A plan may set a longer minimum.

port.description: The TCP port. Converters use many ports (502, 4196, 8886, 8899, ...); no default.

revision.description:
1 at creation, one more with every update; send it back with an update to refuse
overwriting someone else's change.

transport.description: `modbus_tcp`: Modbus TCP to the device. `rtu_over_tcp`: RTU frames over TCP to an RS485 converter; the devices behind one converter (the same host and port on one gateway) share its connection, so they all use this transport and each has its own unit ID.

unit_id.description:
The Modbus unit ID (station number): 0-255 for Modbus TCP, 1-247 for RTU over TCP; 1
when a request leaves it out.

updated_at.description: When the device was last changed.

DeviceId.description:
A device of a tenant (rebuild checklist C2, Laysi/trustiot-v2#100): one Modbus endpoint
a gateway polls, made by the assets service. Unique across tenants; telemetry and the
gateway configuration name the device by it (as text, `protocol::DeviceId`).

Serialized as a lowercase hyphenated UUID string.

created_at.description: When the model was created, by the database clock.

name.description:
The name, unique in the tenant, never changed after creation: 1-40 lowercase letters or
digits in groups joined by single hyphens, starting with a letter.

revision.description:
1 at creation, one more with every update; send it back with an update to refuse
overwriting someone else's change.

updated_at.description: When the model was last changed.

DeviceModelDocument.description:
A device model as a file: what the export downloads and the import uploads. It holds no
IDs, revisions or times, so it can be imported in another tenant or deployment.

format_version.description: The document's version; this release writes and reads 1.

name.description: The model's name, under the naming rule of [`DeviceModel::name`].

DeviceModelId.description:
A device model of a tenant (rebuild checklist C1), made by the assets service; unlike the
model's name, which is unique per tenant only, it is unique across tenants.

Serialized as a lowercase hyphenated UUID string.

DeviceModelList.description: The tenant's device models, by name.

DeviceModelPoint.description: A data point of a device model: how the gateway reads one value, and what the value means.

address.description:
The 0-based protocol address of the first coil or register (40001 in a device manual is
address 0). A point's registers end at 65535 at most and do not overlap another point's
of the same function code.

byte_order.description: Where the bytes of the 32-bit value 0xAABBCCDD end up in the registers: `abcd` big-endian (the default), `badc` bytes swapped in each register, `cdab` registers reversed, `dcba` both.

data_type.description: How the registers decode: `bool` (a bit, or a register that is not 0), `u16`/`i16` (1 register), `u32`/`i32`/`f32` (2), `u64`/`i64`/`f64` (4), `string` (`length` registers of ASCII). Function codes 1 and 2 read `bool` only.

description.description:
What the value means, for people and for the AI features: up to 512 characters, without
control characters other than line feed and tab, format characters, or line and
paragraph separators. Trimmed; empty means none.

function_code.description:
The Modbus read function: 1 coils, 2 discrete inputs, 3 holding registers, 4 input
registers.

key.description:
The key telemetry uses, unique within the model: 1-64 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`
or `-`, starting with a letter or digit.

length.description: For `string` only, which requires it: the number of registers, 2 characters each.

offset.description: Added after `scale`; finite. Numeric types only.

scale.description:
Multiplier applied to the raw number (rebuild checklist F5); finite and not 0. Numeric
types only.

DeviceModelSummary.description: A device model in the tenant's list.

point_count.description: How many data points it has.

updated_at.description: When the model was last changed.

ErrorBody.description:
The JSON body of every error response (M1). Clients ignore fields they do not know, so
fields are only ever added as optional ones.

code.description: What went wrong; clients branch on this.

details.description:
Values the translated message refers to, for example `{"max": 40}`. Never user-facing
text, internal error text, or personal data. Absent when empty.

field_errors.description: The request fields that were rejected. Absent when empty.

message_key.description: The message the client shows, translated by the client.

ErrorCode.description:
What went wrong, as one of a closed set of codes (M1). The HTTP status follows from the
code; a more specific reason goes in the message key, not in a new code.

EventId.description:
An event, unique across services; consumers deduplicate deliveries by it.

Serialized as a lowercase hyphenated UUID string.

EventLogPage.description: One page of the log, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the next, older page; `null` on the last page. Opaque.

FieldError.description: A rejected field of the request body.

details.description: Values the message refers to. Absent when empty.

field.description:
JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) to the rejected value in the request body, for example
`/points/3/address`; an empty string means the whole body.

message_key.description: The message the client shows next to the field.

Gap.description: A spacing between two readings of at least [`GAP_FACTOR`] times the usual one.

from.description: The reading before the gap and the one after it.

GatewayBinding.description: A gateway's binding to a tenant.

binding_id.description: The binding: a new one every time the gateway is bound.

bound_at.description: When it was bound, by the database clock.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the gateway is bound to.

GatewayBindingId.description:
One binding of a gateway to a tenant (rebuild checklist D3, Laysi/trustiot-v2#101), made
by the assets service. A gateway gets a new one every time it is bound, so a binding and
its events always belong to one tenant.

Serialized as a lowercase hyphenated UUID string.

GatewayRegistration.description: A gateway's factory registration, as the service records it.

ca_key_id.description: The issuing CA that signed the initial certificate: the SHA-256 of its public key.

certificate.description:
The initial certificate, PEM: the gateway's MQTT client certificate, subject
`CN=<hardware_id>`, extended key usage client authentication only.

certificate_chain.description:
The initial certificate, then the issuing CA certificate that signed it (the loaded
issuing CA whose key id is `ca_key_id`), PEM: the chain the gateway presents as its MQTT
client certificate. The root is not in it. When that issuing CA is no longer loaded (a
repeat after rotation removed it, services/certs/README.md, "輪替" step 3), the chain is
the initial certificate alone.

endorsement_key_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the endorsement key (its DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo), 64 lower-case hex
digits.

not_after.description:
When the initial certificate expires; the gateway renews it through the renewal endpoint
before then.

not_before.description: When the initial certificate becomes valid.

public_key_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the registered public key (its DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo), 64 lower-case
hex digits.

root_certificate.description:
The root CA certificate, PEM: the gateway's only trust anchor for the MQTT broker's
server certificate (services/certs/README.md, "閘道器對 broker 伺服器憑證的信任"). The
root CRL (Laysi/trustiot-v2#560) can join it here as a new field.

serial.description: The serial number of the initial certificate, lower-case hex.

workstation.description: The name of the workstation that registered it.

IgnoredModels.description:
A stored model list the AI gateway does not use because it no longer fits the
configuration; the role uses its configured models.

reason.description: Why, in English, as the AI gateway explains it (for operators; not translated).

Interval.description: How readings are grouped: `raw` (no grouping) or a bucket length.

IssueWorkstationCertificate.description: The body of `POST /api/certs/v1/workstation-certificates`. Unknown fields are refused.

certificate_request.description:
A PKCS #10 certificate signing request, PEM (`-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----`), at
most 4096 bytes as DER, signed with ecdsa-with-SHA256 by the workstation's ECDSA P-256
key. Only its public key is used, once its signature shows the workstation holds the
private key: the CA decides the subject, the extensions and the validity, and the private
key never leaves the workstation.

workstation.description:
The workstation's name: 1-48 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, starting with a
letter or digit. The certificate's subject is `CN=workstation:<name>`.

Language.description: A language the interface or AI answers may use.

Latest.description: The latest value of each data point of a device that has a reading in the raw period.

earliest.description: The start of the period searched (the raw period), UTC.

points.description: One entry per data point, ordered by data point.

LatestPoint.description: The latest value of one data point.

time.description: When the reading was taken, UTC.

oneOf.description: A person, through the API (a platform administrator too).
A service's own work, such as a scheduled job.
Who made the change; `null` when the producer did not say.

aggregate_seq.description: The event's number within its aggregate, from 1.

aggregate_type.description: What changed: the aggregate's kind, for example `tenant`.

occurred_at.description: When the change happened, by the producer's clock.

payload.description: The event's payload as the producer wrote it, in the version above; a JSON object.

producer.description: The service that wrote the event, for example `identity`.

recorded_at.description: When the event log stored the event, by the database clock.

oneOf.description: The tenant; `null` for a platform-wide event.

LoggedIn.description: The answer to a valid code; the session cookie is in `Set-Cookie`.

LoginRequest.description: The body of `POST /auth/login`: a JSON object that names one of the two steps in `step`. Any other field is refused.

oneOf.description: Step 1: mail a login code to this address.

email.description: The address to log in with.

oneOf.title: send_code

oneOf.description: Step 2: log in with the code from the email.

email.description: The address the code was sent to.

redirect_to.description: Where to go after logging in: a path on this site such as `/devices?page=2`. Default `/`.

oneOf.title: verify_code

MemberRole.description:
A role in a tenant, as the API takes and returns it: setting a member's role, and the tenants
of the current session.

Membership.description: A user's membership of a tenant.

oneOf.description:
The role before this request; `null` when the user was not a member. Equal to `role`
when nothing changed.

MessageKey.description: Key of the translated message the client shows; never the message itself.

ModelProvider.description:
A provider configured in the AI gateway: a role's models may name it when its protocol is
the role's.

name.description: The provider's name, the `<provider>` of a model.

ModelRole.description: A model role of the AI gateway.

configured_models.description: The models the configuration gives the role, which a reset goes back to.

oneOf.description: A stored list that is not in use; `null` when there is none.

models.description: The models in effect, `<provider>/<model>` in fallback order.

protocol.description:
The role's protocol, which only the configuration sets: `anthropic-messages` or
`openai-decisions` today.

updated_at.description:
When the role was last changed or reset; `null` when it never was, or the AI gateway
could not say.

updated_by.description:
Who last changed or reset the role, as the AI gateway recorded it (`user:<user ID>` for
changes made here); `null` when nobody did.

version.description:
The version a change or reset must send as `expected_version`; 0 when the role was never
changed.

ModelRoles.description: Every model role and every configured provider, by name.

ModelSource.description: Where a role's models in effect come from.

PoolGateway.description: A gateway of the device pool.

oneOf.description: Its current binding; `null` while it is bound to no tenant.

hardware_id.description: The hardware ID: the common name of its certificates and its MQTT identity.

pooled_at.description: When the assets service put it in the pool.

registered_at.description: When the certs service registered it at the factory.

workstation.description: The production workstation that registered it.

PoolGatewayList.description: A page of the device pool, by hardware ID (byte order).

next_after.description: The `after` of the next page; `null` on the last one.

ai_language.description: The language AI answers are written in; `auto` answers in the language of the question.

language.description: The interface's language; `auto` follows the browser.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone name such as `Asia/Taipei`, or `auto` to follow the browser.

earliest.description: The start of the queryable period of the table read, at the time of the request.

ends_after_now.description:
Whether the range ends after the request's time (a period still running, such as
`today`): its last bucket is not complete.

from.description:
The range read: `from` inclusive, `to` exclusive. `from` is later than requested when the
request started before the queryable period (`truncated`).

resolution.description:
The aggregate table read: one-minute or one-hour cells. A minimum's or maximum's time is
the start of its cell.

truncated.description: Whether `from` was moved to the start of the queryable period.

tz.description: The time zone the buckets follow; every time in the answer has its offset.

Reading.description: One reading's value, as its type stored it.

oneOf.description: A floating-point reading; `null` for NaN or an infinity.

value.description: A floating-point reading; `null` for NaN or an infinity.

oneOf.description: An integer reading.
A boolean reading.
A text reading.

RegisterGateway.description:
The body of `POST /api/certs/v1/gateway-registrations` (factory registration, rebuild
checklist D1, decision 12). Unknown fields are refused. The request carries the workstation's
signature in the `trustiot-workstation-*` headers; see the certs service's README
("出廠登錄").

certificate_request.description:
A PKCS #10 certificate signing request from the gateway's TPM, PEM (`-----BEGIN
CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----`), at most 4096 bytes as DER, signed with ecdsa-with-SHA256 by
the TPM's ECDSA P-256 key. Its public key is registered and never changes; everything else
in it is ignored.

endorsement_key.description:
The public part of the TPM's endorsement key, PEM (`-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----`, an X.509
SubjectPublicKeyInfo of at most 2048 bytes as DER): RSA of 2048 to 4096 bits, or ECDSA
P-256 or P-384. The workstation reads and checks it before it calls; the service records
it to recognise the TPM.

hardware_id.description:
The gateway's hardware ID, which becomes its identity everywhere: the common name of its
certificates, its MQTT username and the gateway segment of its topics. 1-64 ASCII
letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, starting with a letter or digit. A hardware ID is
registered once, and for now it stays taken after it is decommissioned; whether a
decommissioned hardware ID may be registered again is decided in Laysi/trustiot-v2#115.

Resolution.description: The aggregate table a request reads.

RevocationReason.description:
A reason a workstation certificate can be revoked for: the RFC 5280 CRLReason codes that
apply to an end entity, without `certificateHold` (a revocation here is final).

RevokeWorkstationCertificate.description:
The body of `POST /api/certs/v1/workstation-certificates/{serial}/revoke`. Unknown fields are
refused.

oneOf.description:
Why it is revoked. Absent leaves the reason out of the CRL, as RFC 5280 recommends over
`unspecified`.

earliest.description: The start of the queryable period for this interval at the time of the request.

from.description:
The range queried, `from` inclusive and `to` exclusive, UTC; `from` is later than
requested when the request started before the queryable period.

interval.description: The interval used: the requested one, or the automatic choice.

points.description: The buckets with readings, in time order; buckets without readings are left out.

truncated.description: Whether `from` was moved to the start of the queryable period.

tz.description: The time zone the buckets follow.

SeriesKey.description: One data point of one device.

point.description:
The data point key: 1 to 128 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, starting with a letter or
digit.

SeriesPoint.description: One bucket of a series (for `raw`, one reading).

avg.description: The mean of the numeric values.

count.description: How many readings the bucket holds.

min.description:
The smallest numeric value (a bool counts as 0 or 1); `null` when the bucket holds only
text readings.

time.description: The bucket's start (for `raw`, the reading's time), UTC.

SeriesQuery.description:
A semantic request: which series, which range in which time zone, and the bucket length. The
tenant is the caller's; nothing else can name one.

from.description: The range's start, RFC 3339 with an offset (inclusive), rounded down to the minute.

interval.description: The bucket length; `total` (the default) gives one bucket for the whole range.

period.description:
A period relative to the request's time: `today`, `yesterday`, `this_week`, `last_week`,
`this_month`, `last_month`, `this_year`, `last_year` (whole local periods, weeks from
Monday), `last_<N>_days` (N local days with today, 1 to 366) or `last_<N>_hours` (up to
now, 1 to 72). Either this or `from` and `to`.

to.description: The range's end, RFC 3339 with an offset (exclusive), rounded down to the minute.

tz.description:
An IANA time zone name, such as `Asia/Taipei`: the local hours, days, Monday weeks and
months the buckets and the period follow, and the offset of every time in the answer.

SeriesStatistics.description: A series' statistics over the range.

avg.description: The mean of the numeric readings; for an on/off point, the share of readings that were on.

count.description: Readings in the range, and how many of them are numeric (float, int, bool).

oneOf.description: The first and last reading of the range.
The buckets with the highest and lowest mean (not for `total`).

max.description: The largest value and the start of the cell it was in.

min.description: The smallest value and the start of the cell it was in.

rows.description: The buckets with readings, in time order; buckets without readings are left out.

SeriesUsage.description: A series' usage over the range.

baseline.description:
Whether a reading before the range was found, so the usage up to the first reading in the
range is counted.

oneOf.description: The cumulative check; absent without data.

drops.description:
Drops in the range, each counted as a reset or wrap that started again from 0: each loses
at most the usage of one sampling interval.

oneOf.description: The first and last numeric reading in the range.

gaps.description: Gaps in the range, and the longest.

oneOf.description: The buckets with the highest and lowest usage (not for `total`).

rows.description:
The buckets with readings, in time order; a bucket without readings is left out (unknown,
not zero), and the usage across a gap is in the first bucket after it.

skipped_cells.description: Cells left out because their first or last value was not a finite number.

suspicious_steps.description:
Steps much faster than the series usually rises, and the largest: the total includes them,
and they may be a meter misread.

total.description: The usage over the range; absent unless `status` is `ok`.

SetMemberRole.description:
The body of `PUT /api/identity/v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}/members`. Unknown fields are
ignored. Its `Debug` leaves the address out: it is personal data.

email.description:
The email address of an existing user, compared after trimming and in ASCII lower case,
as logging in compares it.

role.description: The role to give the user in the tenant.

SetRoleModels.description:
The body of `PUT /api/identity/v1/platform/ai/model-roles/{role}`. Unknown fields are
ignored.

expected_version.description:
The role's `version` as the caller read it; the change is refused with 409 when the role
has another version by then.

models.description:
1 to 8 distinct `<provider>/<model>` in fallback order, first choice first, of configured
providers whose protocol is the role's.

series.description: One entry per requested series, in the request's order.

StatisticsRow.description: One bucket of a series' statistics.

min.description:
The smallest, largest and mean numeric value (a bool counts as 0 or 1); `null` when the
bucket holds only text readings.

created_at.description: When the tenant was created, by the database clock.

TenantId.description:
A tenant: one customer organisation; every tenant-scoped row and event carries it.

Serialized as a lowercase hyphenated UUID string.

TenantMembership.description: A tenant the user belongs to, with their role there.

name.description:
The tenant's name; `null` only for a tenant that has no record, which only data written
outside the API has.

role.description: The user's role in the tenant.

TimedReading.description: A reading and when it was taken.

TimedValue.description: A number and the time it belongs to (a bucket's start, or a reading's time).

UpdateDevice.description:
The body of `PUT /api/assets/v1/devices/{device_id}`: the device's settings, which replace
all of the current ones (a field left out takes its default). Unknown fields are refused.

hardware_id.description: If sent, the device's current gateway: a device stays on its gateway.

oneOf.description: If sent, the device's current model: a device keeps its model.

name.description: If sent, the device's current name: names never change.

revision.description:
The revision the client last read (`revision` of the device it read): the update is
refused with 409 when the device changed since. Required.

transport.description: `modbus_tcp`: Modbus TCP to the device. `rtu_over_tcp`: RTU frames over TCP to an RS485 converter; the devices behind one converter (the same host and port on one gateway) share its connection, so they all use this transport and each has its own unit ID.

UpdateDeviceModel.description:
The body of `PUT /api/assets/v1/device-models/{model_id}`: the new data points, which replace
all of the model's. Unknown fields are refused.

name.description: The model's name, if sent, must be its current name: names never change.

points.description: The data points, at most 1000, in order; may be empty.

revision.description:
The revision the client last read (`revision` of the model it read): the update is
refused with 409 when the model changed since, so concurrent editors never overwrite each
other's points unseen. Required.

UpdatePreferences.description:
The body of `PATCH /api/identity/v1/preferences`: the settings to change. A field left out
keeps its value; `null` and unknown fields are refused.

ai_language.description: The language AI answers are written in.

time_zone.description: `auto` or an IANA time zone name, spelled as the tzdb spells it.

series.description: One entry per requested series, in the request's order.

UsageRow.description: One bucket of a series' usage.

after_gap.description: The bucket starts after a gap: its usage includes the usage of the gap.

drops.description: Drops counted as a reset or wrap in the bucket.

suspicious_steps.description:
Steps in the bucket much faster than the series usually rises (a misread or a replaced
meter): the usage includes them.

usage.description: The increase of the counter in the bucket.

UsageStatus.description: Whether a series' usage could be computed.

UserId.description:
A user account; one user can be a member of several tenants.

Serialized as a lowercase hyphenated UUID string.

WorkstationCertificate.description: A workstation certificate as the ledger records it.

ca_key_id.description: The issuing CA that signed it: the SHA-256 of its public key, 64 lower-case hex digits.

certificate.description: The certificate, PEM. It goes to the workstation, which keeps it with its private key.

not_after.description: When it expires; a renewal is another issue request before then.

not_before.description: When it becomes valid: five minutes before it was signed.

oneOf.description: Why it was revoked, when a reason was given.

revoked_at.description: When it was revoked; absent while it is not.

serial.description:
The serial number, lower-case hex (32 digits for the certificates this service signs):
the `{serial}` of the revoke request. Keep it; it is how the certificate is revoked.

200.description: The caller's tenant's models, by name.

403.description: No tenant or no role in it (`permission_denied`).

503.description: The database failed (`unavailable`).

201.description: The model was created; `Location` is its URL.

400.description: The `Content-Type` is not `application/json`, the body is larger than 2 MiB (`device_model.body_too_large`), or it is not a JSON object (`device_model.body_invalid`) (`invalid_request`).

403.description: No tenant, or a role below editor (`permission_denied`).

409.description: The tenant has a model of this name (`conflict`, `device_model.name_taken`).

422.description: A naming or data point rule is broken (`validation_failed`); `field_errors` names each problem with a JSON Pointer and a `device_model.*` key. Nothing was written.

503.description: The service does not know the tenant yet (`device_model.tenant_not_ready`), or the database failed (`unavailable`). Nothing was written.

post.summary: Creates a device model; `assets.device_model_created` is written in the same transaction.

201.description: The model was created; `Location` is its URL.

422.description: A field breaks a rule (`validation_failed`, detail `parameter`: `series`, `tz`, `period`, `from`, or `to` with detail `latest` when it ends too far after now), the answer would have too many rows (`telemetry.too_many_points`), or the query reads or holds too much (`telemetry.query_too_heavy`).

429.description: The tenant's query quota or concurrency limit is used up (`rate_limited`).

503.description: Postgres or ClickHouse failed, or the tenant's ClickHouse account is not as the service creates it (`unavailable`).

504.description: The query ran into its time limit (`timeout`).

200.description: `verify_code`: the code matched. `Set-Cookie` holds the session cookie `__Host-trustiot-session` (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`).

202.description: `send_code`: if a user has the address, a code is on its way. The same answer whether or not one has.

400.description: A query string, a `Content-Type` other than `application/json`, a body over 4096 bytes, or a body that is not one of the two steps; unknown fields such as `password` are refused (`invalid_request`).

401.description: `verify_code`: no usable code for the address, or a wrong code (`unauthenticated`). A code dies after 5 attempts and 10 minutes.

403.description: A cross-site request: `Sec-Fetch-Site` other than `same-origin`, or without it an `Origin` that is not this site's (`permission_denied`, message key `security.cross_site_request`). Checked before anything else; nothing changed.

422.description: The email is not an address (`/email`, `login.email_invalid`), the code is not 8 digits (`/code`, `login.code_invalid`), or `redirect_to` is not a path on this site (`/redirect_to`, `login.redirect_invalid`) (`validation_failed`).

503.description: No usable SMTP relay is configured, too many codes are waiting to be sent, the signing keys have not been read, or the database failed; nothing changed (`unavailable`).
